# R023 — Uniform interior gradient estimates for all finite p >= 3

**Accepted as the first substantial result of the 2026-10-14 ten-additional
campaign.** This is an internal research acceptance, relative to the user's
stipulated pinned OpenAI theorems and the credited classical inputs. It is
not external peer review, a worldwide-priority certificate, or a public
submission. It is additional to the sixteen previously accepted results.

The repaired full proof passed independent Opus review; its contribution
passed a separate Grok review as SUBSTANTIAL; and the complete standalone
manuscript passed a fresh independent Codex mathematical/presentation gate
with no required repair. Parent integration and package verification are
committed at `c5728459`. The parent read the complete reviews and their
limits, checked the exact reviewed bytes, and reran the final verification.

## Exact theorem

For each integer n>=2 there exist alpha_n in (0,1/3] and C_n<infinity
such that, for **every finite p>=3** and **every bounded weak solution**
u in W^(1,p)_loc(B_1 subset R^n) of

    integral |Du|^(p-2) Du . Dphi = 0     (phi in C_c^infinity(B_1)),

the continuous representative belongs to C^(1,alpha_n)(B_(1/2)) and

    ||Du||_(L^infinity(B_(1/2))) + [Du]_(C^(0,alpha_n)(B_(1/2)))
        <= C_n osc_(B_1) u.

Neither constant depends on p or u. There is no assumption about the
original critical set, sign, level-set geometry or boundary data. The
exponent is nonexplicit. The statement does not include 2<p<3, an endpoint
sharp exponent, or the full inhomogeneous p-Laplace conjecture.

## Full proof and the new contribution

The complete proof is the [21-page manuscript](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-manuscript/output/pdf/main.pdf),
PDF SHA256 `bc66e9d14e6d83e8e0a9c579e4856c0a302958af952a1506a5849f5b46875155`.
Its source/build receipt has SHA256
`d689320069f165faeb21cb2f8be63cbf5a70f269b6bf328963dea47b103649a6`.
Historical candidate/pending banners are preserved to keep reviewed bytes
unchanged; this finding and the [parent disposition](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-parent/manuscript-gate-disposition.md)
record the later acceptance. A publication version with author metadata
will require a separately bound build.

The proof first obtains common Lipschitz control and qualitative flatness.
An explicit compact-p Uhlenbeck audit handles bounded p intervals, leaving
p tending to infinity at selected bad scales. The affine lift U(y,b)=u(y)+b
satisfies a different constrained degenerate elliptic equation; the paper
proves the viscosity identity even where Du=0, without asserting that U
is p-harmonic. Its rescaled equations have an effective viscosity.

For finite effective viscosity, an exact transport projection puts every
limit in a fitted isotropic equation, preserving the same fit constant.
Zero viscosity uses the pinned Liouville theorem. Positive viscosity uses
the complete appendix: cone infima, exponential flux, viscosity-to-weak
passage, contact propagation, and fitted-class rigidity. Limit closure
includes both the PDE and every center/radius fit.

For unbounded effective viscosity, the paper constructs one family with
common ellipticity and C2 jet bounds, including degenerate parameter
endpoints. Savin's theorem then gives a proportional Hessian estimate
on an anisotropic coarse cylinder. A quadratic comparison between unequal
fitting parameters retains the coarse slope's size; this is stronger than
the available vector-angle estimate and is needed before invoking that
cylinder estimate. Both branches contradict the selected bad scale.
The pinned geometric derivative extraction yields the common positive
Holder exponent and the stated oscillation bound.

These constrained PDE identifications, projected fit preservation,
uniform rescaled family and unequal-parameter comparison constitute one
substantial bridge. The source infinity theorem, fixed-p regularity,
positive-viscosity technical precursor, Savin theorem and geometric
extraction are credited antecedents, not separate new findings.

## Dependencies and independent gates

- Pinned input: [OpenAI infinity-harmonic manuscript](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb/preprints/Uniform-Interior-C1alpha-Estimates-for-Infinity-Harmonic-Functions-October-4-2026),
  interior regularity, linear lift, zero-viscosity fitted Liouville theorem,
  and equation-free fit/envelope geometry. Its truth is stipulated.
- Classical inputs include Kotschwar–Ni, Uhlenbeck, Julin–Juutinen, Savin,
  linear Harnack, and standard compactness/weak-solution facts. The
  [final source map](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-manuscript-review-r1/source-map.md)
  states actual primary interfaces and reading boundaries; not every
  classical proof has been independently re-proved.
- [Opus round 2](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-proof-r2/review.md):
  PASS for the full repaired four-text proof, resolving R1–R7.
- [Independent contribution review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-contribution-r1/review.md):
  SUBSTANTIAL after comparison with actual primary statements. Its search
  is bounded; worldwide priority is not certified.
- [Independent standalone-manuscript review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-manuscript-review-r1/review.md):
  PASS for the entire frozen manuscript and P1/P3–P8. Parent independently
  verified the P2 archival commit. Review output manifest SHA256:
  `886eb20219722239b7810f20904219ab14bb940fc6117321afe684a1fea596e6`.

## Supporting artifacts and submission limits

The [Lean project](../campaigns/2026-10-14/formal/README.md), pinned to Lean
4.34.1 and mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`, certifies
three scalar and seven vector ellipticity lemmas. The vector theorem
proves both bounds for the actual zero-jet form with sqrt(e), in any real
inner product space under its explicit unit/parameter constraints.
All ten proofs compile from source with only propext, Classical.choice
and Quot.sound. **The PDE, compactness, jet-neighborhood, Savin and full
analytic theorem are not formalized.** The ten lemmas are not ten results.

The [release workflow](../campaigns/2026-10-14/p-gradient-release/README.md)
provides PDF/TeX, reviews, source pins, Lean sources and reproducibility
instructions. A clean extraction passed hash verification and both finite
algebra checkers; a deliberately changed manuscript was rejected. These
checks supplement the written proof, not replace it.

Value-to-gradient convergence and the large-p sharp inhomogeneous transfer
are corollaries of this theorem, with the latter restricted to fixed
p>max(3,1+1/alpha_n) and p-dependent constants. Neither counts separately.
The full [MathDB 405360 problem](https://mathdb.com/p/405360/the-c-p-regularity-conjecture)
is not solved by this finding. No exact matching homogeneous record was
identified in the bounded search. The publication copy lists Myeongjin Kang with no affiliation, CC BY 4.0
for the paper/original prose and MIT for original code/Lean. Third-party
notices are preserved. Final destination/account details remain outstanding. Nothing has
been submitted to Zenodo or MathDB.
records.abstract_tex_exact:
Assuming the interior regularity and fitted-class Liouville results
of the pinned OpenAI infinity-harmonic manuscript, we give an argument
for a dimension-dependent interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate common to
all finite $p\geq3$. The argument uses the exact equation for the
affine lift $u(y)+b$, including at critical points of $u$. Its
anisotropic limits have an effective viscosity. Finite viscosity is
handled by fitted-class rigidity, whose positive-viscosity proof is
included. Infinite viscosity is handled by a uniform small-solution
estimate and a quadratic comparison between different fitting scales.
The exponent is nonexplicit. Supporting Lean files certify the
zero-jet vector ellipticity algebra, not the analytic theorem.

# R024 — Disk rigidity for attained complete polynomial equality

**Accepted as the second substantial result of the 2026-10-14 ten-additional
campaign.** This is internal research acceptance relative to the stipulated
pinned OpenAI inputs and credited geometric theorems, not external peer
review, a worldwide-priority certificate, or a public submission. The
channel, inverse and disk conclusions are accepted as one result.

## Exact theorem

For every finite n,m>=1, every complex n by n matrix A, and every matrix
polynomial F(z)=sum_(k=0)^d z^k C_k with complex m by m coefficients and
arbitrary finite degree, use Euclidean operator norms and the base-first
evaluation F[A]=sum_(k=0)^d A^k tensor C_k. Set

    M = max_(z in W(A)) ||F(z)||.

If M>0 and ||F[A]||=2M, then W(A) is a nondegenerate closed disk.
No rank-one, simple supporting eigenvalue, initial boundary smoothness,
initial irreducibility, or dimension bound is imposed.

Normalize F by M. For every irreducible reducing block B attaining two,
there are fixed coefficient subspaces E,G of the same positive rank r,
isometries U,V onto them, and a polynomial J(z)=V*F(z)U such that F(z)E
is contained in G for every complex z and J is unitary on the boundary
of K=W(B). Its inverse Q is rational, holomorphic throughout the exterior
of K, continuous on its boundary, and tends to zero at infinity. The
nonconstant polynomial f=det J satisfies both full level identities

    {z: |f(z)|<1} = interior K,    {z: |f(z)|=1} = boundary K.

These conclusions do not assert a scalar coefficient compression of the
specified witness. Arbitrary rational or holomorphic witnesses,
nonattained complete suprema, quantitative gaps, stability, and a
classification of disk matrices are outside the claim.

## Proof and contribution

The full proof is the [11-page manuscript](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-manuscript/output/pdf/main.pdf).
PDF SHA256: `ec3b4818c147ae4fefcf9c46760a2a621e1503e3ea025cbbf748405f379eaa8a`.
TeX SHA256: `e90c6cb16bc5bbce03eeaebfd8d8f5c17f77059985a41c7404478db80a2ce609`.
Its source map distinguishes stipulated operations, reproduced inherited
arguments, new deductions, and credited geometric inputs. Preparation-time
status text is preserved to keep every reviewed byte unchanged; this record
and the later parent dispositions state the integrated decision.

The manuscript reproduces dimension-independent exterior boundary
convergence and residual extraction from the earlier equality mechanism.
The new argument retains the Jensen deficit in finite diagonal dual tests,
taking the finite-test limit before the moving-domain limit. A triple
Hilbert-valued variance identity and Fatou then force the diagonal fields
to be constant. Positivity on a curved boundary arc supplies the needed
strictness without limiting marginal identities or a uniform spectral gap.

Trace rationalization gives a denominator with no exterior or boundary
zeros. The residual Gram system has arbitrary positive rank. An ordered
constant test and equality in Parseval produce fixed coefficient spaces
and the full boundary channel identity. Restricting before inversion gives
Q=(1/2) S_E^(-1) U* Mcal^T V, with the ordinary transpose and the indicated
left Gram inverse. Its decay gives the entire determinant sublevel set,
excluding extra exterior components. Noncriticality and the Hermitian
tangent determinant pay the full interface of Jin's circle criterion;
convex polynomial lemniscates alone are not claimed to be circles.
The resulting determinant monomial confines inactive reducing blocks to
the same disk, restoring the full original numerical range.

R016, its dimension-five technical continuation, and the rank-two disk
witness R019 are antecedents. The new arbitrary-rank bridge extends beyond
their scalarization range. Jin's scalar rigidity and the ACV complete
dimension-three result are separately credited. The contribution review
classifies the entire package as SUBSTANTIAL after a bounded primary-source
comparison; it does not establish universal novelty or priority.

## Independent gates and validation

- [Full proof review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-proof-r1/review.md):
  PASS, no required repair. SHA256
  `c1b09f8ad9d05d4b0d323079871b4cfb1e0f2084b41b6e5b0d07f8029288c6c7`.
- [Separate contribution review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-contribution-r1/review.md):
  SUBSTANTIAL for one package, bounded coverage. SHA256
  `d317e565614f3babf2c03e5c6e7b5f4980c31ab28f7e2059b01adc1c8f932df5`.
- [Fresh manuscript review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-manuscript-review-r1/review.md):
  PASS for every original quantifier and the stronger active-block package;
  no required mathematical or layout repair. SHA256
  `35f67ec7bd5d885c4ccd2c2230d694faaa85eb5fa5657ae828b21e91b9a99ce0`.

The parent read the complete proof/manuscript reviews and manuscript,
checked the source interfaces and frozen hashes, reproduced the 17+16
exact supporting checks, and inspected all eleven PDF pages. The final
review separately reconstructed the proof, checked 52 source-map line
targets, reproduced the finite checks and inspected every page. An
optional scalar-maximum/zeroth-coefficient notation collision is harmless
in context and is documented rather than changing the frozen paper.

The pinned input revision is `openai/math@fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`.
The complete inequality and Faber operations are stipulated true. Jin's
Lemma 8 and Proposition 6 are credited external inputs with their exact
interfaces stated, not new theorems of this package. The paper and source
map expose these dependencies.

## Publication and formal coverage

The [local release workflow](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-release/README.md)
packages the reviewed PDF/TeX, provenance, independent reviews, exact
checkers, all-page QA, and a portable hash/check verifier. Its archive
receipt records clean-extraction verification. Author: Myeongjin Kang,
no affiliation; original prose CC BY 4.0, original code MIT. Third-party
rights are preserved. Historical third-party source copies are excluded.

**No full Lean certificate exists.** The 33 exact finite checks exercise
Gram restrictions, inverse multiplication order, transpose and half
factors, and variance orientation, including deliberate mutations. They
do not establish the conformal, Hilbert-valued, Fatou, rationalization,
maximum-principle or geometric arguments. GLM's finite real scalar variance
implementation has now passed the [independent parent audit](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-formal-review-r1/review.md).
The generic identity, per-column identity and nonnegative-deficit corollary
compile on Lean 4.34.1 and pinned mathlib with only propext, Classical.choice
and Quot.sound. A [portable Lake project](../campaigns/2026-10-14/matrix-disk-formal-v1/README.md)
and exact source/audit receipts supplement the updated archive. This does
not retroactively supply a formal proof of the analytic argument and earns
no separate accepted-result credit.

Nothing has been submitted to Zenodo or MathDB. The local MathDB routing
draft distinguishes this equality theorem from the credited complete
inequality in record 392465. No public URL, DOI or endorsement is invented.
records.abstract_tex_exact:
Relative to the pinned complete Crouzeix inequality and its exterior Faber
operations, and to Jin's geometric circle criterion, we prove that actual
factor-two equality for one finite matrix-valued polynomial forces the
numerical range to be a nondegenerate disk in every finite dimension.
We retain the Jensen deficit in finite diagonal dual tests. Strong exterior
boundary convergence and a triple-variance Fatou argument then make the
diagonal compressed resolvents constant, without a rank-one assumption.
An ordered constant test and equality in Parseval produce a fixed
matrix polynomial channel that is unitary on the boundary. Its rational
inverse is holomorphic in the exterior and vanishes at infinity. The
determinant therefore realizes the boundary as a full polynomial level
set. The numerical-range Hermitian tangent pencil supplies the additional
hypothesis of the credited circle criterion. The argument allows coefficient
rank greater than one and assumes no initial boundary smoothness.

# R025 — Functional hard-sphere fluctuations on a regular Boltzmann lifespan

**Accepted as the third substantial result of the 2026-10-14 ten-additional
campaign.** This is internal research acceptance relative to the stipulated
pinned source interfaces, not external peer review or a worldwide-priority
certificate. The shrinking-window estimate and path-space conclusion count
as one result.

## Exact theorem and dependencies

Consider deterministic elastic hard spheres of diameter epsilon in
three-dimensional whole space, with activity mu = epsilon^(-2). The initial
grand-canonical law is proportional to

    mu^N/N! 1_{|x_i-x_j|>epsilon} product_i f_0(x_i,v_i) dZ_N,
    N = 0,1,2,... .

Let f_0 be a smooth probability density. For some beta>0 assume that both
f_0 and its spatial gradient have finite norm

    ||g||_{Bol,2beta} = sum_{a in Z^3} sup_{|x-a|<=1,v} exp(2beta|v|^2)|g(x,v)|.

Assume a nonnegative classical Boltzmann solution on the entire prescribed
finite interval [0,T], T>0, with a uniform exp(2beta|v|^2) bound. Relative
to the finite-history interfaces of the pinned source, for every finite
list of real compactly supported smooth tests on R^6, the vector of fields

    X_t^epsilon(phi) = mu^(-1/2)(sum_i phi(z_i(t)) - E sum_i phi(z_i(t)))

converges in D([0,T],R^d), with the Skorokhod J1 topology, to the continuous
Gaussian field of the credited finite-dimensional theorem. The sequence
is C-tight. The covariance, backward propagator, weak linearized drift and
collision-noise form are specified in equations (1.6)–(1.8) of the paper;
the initial covariance is integral f_0 phi psi, without a fixed-number
subtraction.

The result concerns the actual unsmoothed gas with exact microscopic
centering throughout the supplied interval. It adds no equilibrium,
periodicity, smallness, resampling, shortened-lifespan or global-existence
assumption. It does not assert weak convergence in the uniform-topology
Borel space on all of D. The operational source assumptions are stated in
Section 2; their truth is stipulated at
`openai/math@fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`.

## Proof and contribution

The complete [19-page manuscript](../campaigns/2026-10-14/kinetic-manuscript-consolidation/output/pdf/main.pdf)
has PDF SHA256 `08a092590559fa81c1d2c759e06efb9a03b1e7b6ede1d708ace731cc0f2028dc`
and TeX SHA256 `f2548882cf47aa4259c68b43ea38d755c395b47008300783856788ab5ef6fd38`.

One collective time translation of a connected history supplies a
shrinking-window factor at the sharp factorial-cumulant scale, including
redundant contacts whose times are determined rather than independent
coordinates. The repaired construction retains a prefix-measurable global
chronology indicator through the translation and flux-tree bound. Initial
links retain their connected activity scale. A fixed Gaussian reserve
keeps summability independent of later moment order. A decorated final-slab
kernel controls the number of jumping particles. Together with credited
moment, continuity, chaining and centering arguments, these estimates give
the full unsmoothed path-space conclusion.

Short-time nonequilibrium and long-time equilibrium process theorems of
Bodineau–Gallagher–Saint-Raymond–Simonella, the regular-lifespan framework
of Deng–Hani–Ma, the pinned finite-dimensional theorem, and the earlier
project's continuity and centering arguments are antecedents. They are
identified in the paper and source map. The separate contribution review
judges the new bridge SUBSTANTIAL within its recorded literature search;
this is not an exhaustive priority determination.

## Independent gates and validation

- [Proof round 2](../campaigns/2026-10-14/kinetic-proof-r2/review.md): PASS
  after the extended-history chronology repair; full original scope.
- [Contribution review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/kinetic-contribution-r1/review.md):
  SUBSTANTIAL for the new path-space bridge, conditional on proof validity.
- [Original manuscript review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/kinetic-manuscript-review-r1/review.md):
  PASS with seven nonblocking corrections, all addressed in the consolidated edition.
- [Final manuscript review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/kinetic-manuscript-review-r2/review.md):
  PASS for that edition, SHA256
  `feddd8af34f64fc0f856f3b2ca97a1f5a0ed9c3cdf55c36cffd737a539cbb396`.
  Six remaining editorial clarifications are retained in the included parent
  companion without altering reviewed manuscript bytes.

The parent authenticated the corrected paper's 107 input and 57 output
records, checked the exact editorial diff, reproduced its 213 structural
checks and inspected all 19 rendered pages. Final review authenticated
71 inputs and two outputs. The final archive passed clean-extraction
verification: all 208 project files, exact membership, hashes and gate
bindings, plus byte-identical receipts from five finite-check programs.
These checks support the analytic proof; they do not replace it.

## Publication materials and formal coverage

Author: **Myeongjin Kang**, no affiliation. Original paper/prose: CC BY 4.0;
original code/Lean: MIT. Third-party rights remain intact. The local archive

records.acceptance_record_text:
# R026 — An integral regular summand in every staircase Specht tensor cube

**Accepted as the fourth substantial result of the 2026-10-14 ten-additional
campaign.** This is internal research acceptance after separate proof,
contribution, manuscript and scoped formal reviews. It is not external peer
review, an exhaustive priority determination, or a public submission. The
integral and every-ring conclusions constitute one result.

## Exact theorem

For every integer m >= 1, put N=m(m+1)/2, rho=(m,m-1,...,1),
B={(i,j): i,j>=1, i+j<=m+1}, and G=Sym(B). In the common word realization
of the integral Specht lattice S_Z^rho, define v_R and v_C by alternating
the letters 1,...,r on each row and column of length r, respectively.
Rows are ordered left to right and columns top to bottom, as specified in
Section 2 of the paper. Set L=(S_Z^rho) tensor (S_Z^rho) tensor (S_Z^rho)
and z=v_R tensor v_R tensor v_C, with diagonal left G-action.

The map I: Z[G] -> L given by delta_g -> gz has an explicit integral
G-linear left inverse P. Thus its N! orbit vectors form a basis of a split
regular summand. For every commutative unital ring A, including nonflat
extensions and the zero ring, the scalar-extended maps give a split
A[G]-embedding into (S_A^rho) tensor_A (S_A^rho) tensor_A (S_A^rho), where
S_A^rho=A tensor_Z S_Z^rho. No factorial is inverted and no characteristic
restriction is imposed.

Explicitly, let beta(i,j)=m+2-i-j, b0(i,j)=j, and let theta* extract the
coefficient of (e_beta,e_b0,e_beta) in ambient tensor-word coordinates.
Then

    P(x) = sum_(g in G) theta*(g^(-1)x) delta_g.

The paper proves that this agrees on every basis triple with
J^(-1) pi_D q^B, where q(a,b,c)=0 unless a=c and otherwise returns the
letter (a+b-1,a), D={(r,a):1<=a<=r<=m}, and J identifies the distinct-letter
orbit with the regular module. The surviving term has coefficient +1.
The theorem supplies lower bounds on regular multiplicities, not exact
multiplicities of the entire tensor cube.

## Proof, sources and contribution boundary

The complete [six-page manuscript](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-manuscript/main.pdf)
has PDF SHA256 `40aebbdda3c407298f499895b7cd8aee543025864efbcb94808441e1b6b6f54c`
and TeX SHA256 `015e76c58ebbd6b92c8868d2de9cf49f533f18408e5017b720df8d02f4767495`.
It proves the integral polytabloid identification, equivariance, coordinate
formula, integer square-deficit support elimination, palette induction,
positive unit sign, splitting and arbitrary base change as a standalone
argument.

Bryant–Kovács' separating-product mechanism, Ikenmeyer's triangular
uniqueness, and the pinned cyclic-polytabloid square-deficit construction
are credited ingredients. The new conclusion is the integral and
every-characteristic regular summand. Complex regular containment is an
antecedent from the pinned complex surjection and Harman–Ryba, or from
I21's stronger intermediate isomorphism and Harman–Ryba. Characteristic-2
projective-indecomposable occurrence is also already known. These are not
additional contributions, and the specified generator alone earns no
separate novelty claim.

The contribution review judges the package SUBSTANTIAL narrowly within
its recorded primary-literature comparison, particularly for regular
multiplicities and the unrestricted positive-characteristic conclusion.
It makes no worldwide-priority guarantee. OpenAI inputs are accepted at
`fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`; the paper reproduces the integral
arguments and does not use complex constituent coverage to infer modular
splitting. It does not transfer field-level injectivity of the regular
module to the integers.

## Independent gates and validation

- [Proof review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-proof-r1/review.md): PASS
  for the full original all-m and every-ring theorem, with no repairs.
- [Contribution review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-contribution-factory-r1/review.md):
  SUBSTANTIAL narrowly, with attribution requirements implemented in the paper.
- [Full manuscript review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-manuscript-review-r1/review.md):
  PASS with no paper edits required, SHA256
  `2b9d5470d96c0f334eed1073489b94c13296fea12924acb096fdb26850184d76`.
- [Scoped Lean review](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-formal-review-r1/review.md):
  PASS with no repairs, SHA256
  `92b21ed40425c72be41c00a4eb65e2d349b33e8dfeffe3bbb930067cbe30b254`.

The parent authenticated the reviews and frozen paper, read the complete
manuscript and checked every rendered page. The independent manuscript
review rebuilt a byte-identical PDF and added nine finite control groups;
the parent reproduced their complete receipt on a copy. These cover
polytabloids, projection, the orbit identity, coordinate equivalence,
palette and deficit checks, hook divisibility, the complex antecedent and
mutations. Such finite tests support the proof; they do not prove all m.

Both final-package conditions are satisfied: the full cited I21 note is
included at its exact hash with a rights notice, and an actual scoped
formal-coverage supplement explains the completed audit and omissions.
Ten optional editorial clarifications are embedded in the included parent
disposition without changing reviewed manuscript bytes.

## Formal coverage and release

**The full staircase theorem is not formalized in Lean.** Sixteen supporting
theorems prove the conditional finite-group coordinate splitting and its
equivariance, injectivity and invariant complement, scalar extension of
given split/intertwining maps without flatness, and the integer zero-deficit
implication. The staircase-specific separation identity is an explicit
unproved instance, not a formalized theorem. Polytabloids, palettes, support
budget, positive unit sign, the all-m instance and multiplicity conclusions
remain prose proofs. The independent audit adds eighteen review theorems,
including noncommutative and nonflat examples, and rejects three source
mutations. Fresh-source compilation uses Lean 4.34.1 and pinned mathlib
with only standard axioms; dependencies and compiler remain trusted setup.

Author: **Myeongjin Kang**, no affiliation. Original prose CC BY 4.0;
original code MIT; third-party notices retained. The [release workflow](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-release/README.md)
prepares local Zenodo/MathDB drafts and reproducible source materials.
Earlier pending/count fields in frozen preparation records are historical.
This acceptance record and the included final parent disposition supply
the later state. No DOI, public paper URL, MathDB record or external
endorsement is claimed.

The verified local archive is
`output/release/r026-integral-staircase-regular-summand-v1.zip`,
1,085,619 bytes, SHA256
`c371bc4461d5c40b701e3f5445ccd664a1c8f8184b537544a117f2b73c92f42b`.
It contains 172 project files plus its bundle manifest. Clean extraction

See the [final receipt](../campaigns/2026-10-14/staircase-parent/final-package-verification.json).
Nothing has been publicly uploaded or submitted.

# R027 — The ordinary crossing number of the complete graph minus an edge

**Accepted as the fifth substantial result of the 2026-10-14 ten-additional
campaign.** This is internal acceptance under the stipulated pinned upstream
theorems, after independent proof, contribution, manuscript and scoped formal
reviews. It is not external peer review or a worldwide priority certificate.
The path-product application is part of this one result.

For every integer n >= 2 and every edge e of K_n, put

    Z(n) = floor(n/2) floor((n-1)/2) floor((n-2)/2) floor((n-3)/2) / 4.

Then the ordinary crossing number is

    cr(K_n - e) = Z(n) - binom(floor((n-1)/2), 2)
                = floor((n+2)/2) floor((n-1)/2) floor((n-3)/2) floor((n-4)/2) / 4.

There is no restriction to straight, convex, rectilinear or two-page drawings
in the lower bound. For every m >= 4 and n >= 1, with P_n the path of n edges,

    cr(K_m box P_n) = (n-1) cr(K_(m+2) - e) + 2 Z(m+1)
      = floor((m+1)/2) floor((m-1)/2) floor((m-2)/2)
        [n floor((m+4)/2) + floor((m-4)/2)] / 4.

records.abstract_tex_exact:
We prove that for every integer $n\ge 2$ and every edge $e$ of the complete graph $K_n$, the ordinary crossing number of $K_n-e$ is
\[
\crn(K_n-e)=\frac14\Big\lfloor\frac{n+2}{2}\Big\rfloor\Big\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\Big\rfloor\Big\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\Big\rfloor\Big\lfloor\frac{n-4}{2}\Big\rfloor ,
\]
which was conjectured by Zheng, Lin, Yang and Cui in 2007. The proof relies on the September~2026 OpenAI preprint proving the Harary--Hill formula for $\crn(K_n)$, whose stated results we use without re-proving them. Given that formula, the even orders follow from a theorem of Ouyang, Wang and Huang (2014), equivalently of Chia and Lee (2015), and the odd orders $n\le 13$ follow from their counting bound and integrality. The new content is the lower bound for odd $n\ge 15$. We adapt the polynomial rank method of the OpenAI preprint to the missing edge. The adaptation restricts the test polynomials so that they put no weight on the missing pair. It pairs two different vanishing subspaces by mixed orthogonality. It also localizes, with a twisted detector that needs the full rectangular nonsingularity statement of the preprint, only at the vertices whose stars are complete. Via the product identity of Ouyang, Wang and Huang, the formula gives the crossing number of $K_m\,\square\,P_n$ conjectured by Zheng et al.\ for all $m\ge 4$ and $n\ge 1$, where $P_n$ is the path with $n$ edges. The new lower-bound input enters this consequence for odd $m\ge 13$ and $n\ge2$; the literature comparison is bounded as stated in Section~\ref{sec:novelty}.

records.abstract_plain_text: We prove that for every integer n >= 2 and every edge e of the complete graph K_n, the ordinary crossing number is cr(K_n-e) = (1/4) floor((n+2)/2) floor((n-1)/2) floor((n-3)/2) floor((n-4)/2), which was conjectured by Zheng, Lin, Yang and Cui in 2007. The proof relies on the September 2026 OpenAI preprint proving the Harary–Hill formula for cr(K_n), whose stated results we use without re-proving them. Given that formula, the even orders follow from a theorem of Ouyang, Wang and Huang (2014), equivalently of Chia and Lee (2015), and the odd orders n <= 13 follow from their counting bound and integrality. The new content is the lower bound for odd n >= 15. We adapt the polynomial rank method of the OpenAI preprint to the missing edge. The adaptation restricts the test polynomials so that they put no weight on the missing pair. It pairs two different vanishing subspaces by mixed orthogonality. It also localizes, with a twisted detector that needs the full rectangular nonsingularity statement of the preprint, only at the vertices whose stars are complete. Via the product identity of Ouyang, Wang and Huang, the formula gives the crossing number of K_m square P_n conjectured by Zheng et al. for all m >= 4 and n >= 1, where P_n is the path with n edges. The new lower-bound input enters this consequence for odd m >= 13 and n >= 2; the literature comparison is bounded as stated in the novelty section of the paper.

This is an AI-assisted preprint with internal independent agent proof, contribution and manuscript reviews, not external peer review. Supporting Lean material is partial and does not formalize the complete theorem. Mathematical results from OpenAI/math at revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb are stipulated premises, with exact source interfaces and other credited inputs disclosed in the paper. The literature comparison is bounded and does not certify worldwide priority.

Formal coverage: 47 supporting Lean theorems and 17 definitions cover finite tensor kernels, dimensions, diagonal nondegeneracy, mixed tests, twisted detection, localization budgets and conditional descent. Drawing topology, concrete substitutions, divisibility, instantiated descent/injections, orientation/count comparison, even/upper assembly and product theorem remain prose. U4 is an explicit premise, not a proved upstream theorem or new axiom.
